react_result.final_narrative_text: The differentially abundant metabolite set is dominated by tryptophan-derived intermediates that span three functionally distinct branches of the tryptophan metabolism network (KEGG:hsa00380 / WP:WP465 / MUMM:tryptophan_metabolism). This pathway achieved universal rank-1 consensus across all three independent enrichment paradigms — RaMP ORA (FDR 5.6×10⁻¹⁸, 7/54 metabolites hit), MetaboAnalystR PSEA (p 1.59×10⁻⁸, 6/41 metabolites hit), and Mummichog m/z-direct analysis (p 0.0016, 11/18 metabolites hit) — with no structural InChIKey conflicts among the nine canonical ChEBI IDs. The serotonergic arm (tryptophan → tryptamine → serotonin → melatonin) was the most densely covered, with L-tryptophan (C00078), serotonin (C00780), and melatonin (C01598) confirmed in every tool. The kynurenine-NAD⁺ arm contributed quinolinic acid (C03722) and 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid (C00632), the latter bridging immune regulation and oxidative stress. Indoleacetaldehyde (C00637) and the arginase-family intermediate 1-pyrroline-5-carboxylic acid (C03912) confirmed that indole-acetaldehyde diversion and glutamate-semialdehyde shunting are also active. Serotonin (C00780) is the primary downstream driver, connecting the tryptophan pool to melatonin synthesis via AANAT and ASMT, while quinolinic acid (C03722) anchors the neuroactive NAD⁺-precursor branch with established excitotoxicity implications. The breadth of hits across both neurotransmitter and immune-metabolism arms suggests the treatment perturbation coordinately dysregulates tryptophan allocation between serotonergic signaling and kynurenine-pathway energy/redox metabolism.

react_result.final_narrative_text: Tryptophan metabolism is the overwhelmingly dominant affected pathway across all three orthogonal enrichment paradigms. RaMP multi-DB ORA returned KEGG:map00380 'Tryptophan metabolism' as the top hit with FDR=5.6e-18 and fold enrichment=778, covering 7 of 10 input metabolites; the same pathway appeared as rank-4 'Tryptophan catabolism leading to NAD+ production' (FDR=1.5e-10) and rank-9 'Serotonin and melatonin biosynthesis' (FDR=3.4e-08, Reactome R-HSA-209931). Mummichog m/z-direct activity scored 'Tryptophan metabolism' (MUMM:tryptophan_metabolism) as its sole significant hit at p=0.0017 with near-complete overlap (17 of 18 pathway metabolites matched). MetaboAnalystR PSEA confirmed KEGG:hsa00380 at p=1.59e-08, rank 1. L-Tryptophan (C00078) is the canonical entry-point substrate; its catabolism funnels into the serotonin/melatonin branch (serotonin C00780, melatonin C01598, tryptamine C00398, indoleacetaldehyde C00637) and the kynurenine/quinolinate branch (quinolinic acid C03722, 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid C00632). 1-Pyrroline-5-carboxylic acid (C03912) reflects parallel proline-glutamate semialdehyde interconversion. L-Valine (C00183) is a secondary hit in branched-chain amino acid biosynthesis (KEGG:hsa00290, p=0.044). The convergence of ORA, m/z-network, and PSEA on the same biochemical module with 7 shared driver metabolites and FDR spanning 1.6e-08 to 5.6e-18 establishes tryptophan metabolism as the central biological narrative. Limitations: two tools (FELLA, SSPA) were unavailable, and the downstream enzymatic step connecting 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid to quinolinate phosphoribosyltransferase (EC 2.4.2.19) was not directly confirmed by the enrichment outputs.

  "narrative_text": "Three independent pathway-analysis paradigms converge on tryptophan metabolism (KEGG:hsa00380) as the dominant affected pathway in this differential metabolomics dataset. RaMP multi-DB ORA returned KEGG:map00380 / Tryptophan metabolism at rank 1 (FDR = 5.56e-18, 7 of 10 input metabolites mapped, fold enrichment 778), with the same pathway confirmed in WikiPathways (WP:WP465), Reactome serotonin/melatonin biosynthesis (R-HSA-209931), and the IDO metabolic pathway (WP:WP5414). MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA independently scored hsa00380 at p = 1.59e-08 with 6 input metabolites, the strongest signal by more than three orders of magnitude over the next hit. Mummichog m/z-network enrichment ranked tryptophan metabolism first (p = 0.00185, 17/18 metabolites overlapping) and additionally surfaced arginine and proline metabolism (rank 2, p = 0.030) via the pyrroline-hydroxycarboxylic acid entry, suggesting a partial proline-cycle contribution alongside the dominant tryptophan signal. The driver metabolites are L-tryptophan (canonical substrate), serotonin (neurotransmitter branch), melatonin (pinecal output), and 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid (kynurenine/nicotinate branch), all of which appear in RaMP metabolites_hit for both the KEGG and WikiPathways pathway instances. The serotonin-and-melatonin biosynthesis sub-pathway (R-HSA-209931) reflects the shared tryptophan origin of both metabolites. Tryptophan hydroxylase (TPH) and aromatic L-amino acid decarboxylase (AADC) are the key enzymes linking L-tryptophan to serotonin, with acetylserotonin N-methyltransferase (ASMT) completing the melatonin arm. L-Valine appears as a single-hit outlier in valine/leucine/isoleucine biosynthesis (MetaboAnalystR rank 2, p = 0.044) and does not drive the primary tryptophan signal. react_result.final_narrative_text: Three independent pathway-analysis paradigms converge on tryptophan metabolism (KEGG:hsa00380) as the dominant affected pathway in this differential metabolomics dataset. RaMP multi-DB ORA returned KEGG:map00380 / Tryptophan metabolism at rank 1 (FDR = 5.56e-18, 7 of 10 input metabolites mapped, fold enrichment 778), with the same pathway confirmed in WikiPathways (WP:WP465), Reactome serotonin/melatonin biosynthesis (R-HSA-209931), and the IDO metabolic pathway (WP:WP5414). MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA independently scored hsa00380 at p = 1.59e-08 with 6 input metabolites, the strongest signal by more than three orders of magnitude over the next hit. Mummichog m/z-network enrichment ranked tryptophan metabolism first (p = 0.00185, 17/18 metabolites overlapping) and additionally surfaced arginine and proline metabolism (rank 2, p = 0.030) via the pyrroline-hydroxycarboxylic acid entry, suggesting a partial proline-cycle contribution alongside the dominant tryptophan signal. The driver metabolites are L-tryptophan (canonical substrate), serotonin (neurotransmitter branch), melatonin (pinecal output), and 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid (kynurenine/nicotinate branch), all of which appear in RaMP metabolites_hit for both the KEGG and WikiPathways pathway instances. The serotonin-and-melatonin biosynthesis sub-pathway (R-HSA-209931) reflects the shared tryptophan origin of both metabolites. Tryptophan hydroxylase (TPH) and aromatic L-amino acid decarboxylase (AADC) are the key enzymes linking L-tryptophan to serotonin, with acetylserotonin N-methyltransferase (ASMT) completing the melatonin arm. L-Valine appears as a single-hit outlier in valine/leucine/isoleucine biosynthesis (MetaboAnalystR rank 2, p = 0.044) and does not drive the primary tryptophan signal. Quinolinic acid is captured in the tryptophan kynurenine branch by RaMP but falls below the MetaboAnalystR significance threshold, reflecting the more stringent single-metabolite test in that tool.

final_react_result.final_narrative_text: The differentially abundant metabolite set is dominated by tryptophan-derived intermediates that span three functionally distinct branches of the tryptophan metabolism network (KEGG:hsa00380 / WP:WP465 / MUMM:tryptophan_metabolism). This pathway achieved universal rank-1 consensus across all three independent enrichment paradigms — RaMP ORA (FDR 5.6×10⁻¹⁸, 7/54 metabolites hit), MetaboAnalystR PSEA (p 1.59×10⁻⁸, 6/41 metabolites hit), and Mummichog m/z-direct analysis (p 0.0016, 11/18 metabolites hit) — with no structural InChIKey conflicts among the nine canonical ChEBI IDs. The serotonergic arm (tryptophan → tryptamine → serotonin → melatonin) was the most densely covered, with L-tryptophan (C00078), serotonin (C00780), and melatonin (C01598) confirmed in every tool. The kynurenine-NAD⁺ arm contributed quinolinic acid (C03722) and 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid (C00632), the latter bridging immune regulation and oxidative stress. Indoleacetaldehyde (C00637) and the arginase-family intermediate 1-pyrroline-5-carboxylic acid (C03912) confirmed that indole-acetaldehyde diversion and glutamate-semialdehyde shunting are also active. Serotonin (C00780) is the primary downstream driver, connecting the tryptophan pool to melatonin synthesis via AANAT and ASMT, while quinolinic acid (C03722) anchors the neuroactive NAD⁺-precursor branch with established excitotoxicity implications. The breadth of hits across both neurotransmitter and immune-metabolism arms suggests the treatment perturbation coordinately dysregulates tryptophan allocation between serotonergic signaling and kynurenine-pathway energy/redox metabolism.
